Class Swerve

java.lang.Object
com.ctre.phoenix6.swerve.SwerveDrivetrain<TalonFX,TalonFX,CANcoder>
frc.robot.subsystems.swerve.Swerve
All Implemented Interfaces:
AutoCloseable, Subsystem
public class Swerve extends SwerveDrivetrain<TalonFX,TalonFX,CANcoder> implements Subsystem
FM's swerve drivetrain: Phoenix 6's SwerveDrivetrain for control and 250 Hz odometry, with the robot pose owned by PoseFusion on the main loop so it can be replayed.

Where the pose comes from

CTRE's odometry thread still runs every module at 250 Hz. Its telemetry callback, on that thread, only copies each sample into a bounded queue. Each robot loop periodic() drains the queue into SwerveInputs, records it with AdvantageKit, and hands every sample to PoseFusion, which is the pose everything on the robot reads (getRobotPose()). Vision measurements go to PoseFusion too (see Vision). CTRE's internal estimate is kept aligned with the fused pose (syncCtrePose()) because its field-centric requests rotate by its own heading.

From the 2026 offseason branch

Per-module current and connection logging at 10 Hz, the SwerveAlignment encoder publisher, skipping the bus optimisation on a dead bus (CanConfigBudget), and never doing log work on CTRE's odometry thread. FM's own drive modes (pilot aim at target through ShotCalculator) are kept from main; the offseason bot's turret-pivot mode is not.

Simulation

maple-sim has no WPILib 2027 build, so the sim is CTRE's own updateSimState. To give the vision comparison something to do, the sim keeps a separate perfect truth odometry and feeds the robot code a version with wheel-radius and gyro-drift error (Swerve.SimErrors).

      public void updateInputs()
      Reads the drivetrain into inputs, records them, and integrates this loop's odometry into the fused pose. Called by Robot at the top of every loop, before vision and before the scheduler, so everything this loop sees the same pose.

    • logBatteryUsage

      protected void logBatteryUsage()
      Reports drive and steer supply current to the battery logger every loop and logs per-module and summed currents at 10 Hz. Diagnostic outputs only; nothing decides on them, so they are read straight from the signals rather than through SwerveInputs.
